_comment: CHURN CARD — SLIP-AWARE eq34 ELECTION, 3 h field arm.  One functional key over
knobs (v3/v4/v5) is armed — this is a Card-3/4 CORRECTNESS mechanism on a different
axis and mixing it with a D5 treatment would make neither readable.
WHAT IT DOES.  A slipped arc is kept OUT of the eq34 spanning tree wherever the graph
allows: a slipped incumbent loses its sticky seed, and a slipped arc is refused in the
new-edge walk's FIRST pass (the same two-pass shape INC-1 uses for cold hosts) and
admitted only in the second.  A slipped TREE edge refloats every fundamental cycle that
closes through it; a slipped CHORD costs exactly one DD.
THE NUMBER THIS ARM EXISTS FOR: eq34_slip_readmitted / eq34_slip_deseeded.  Near 0 means
the graph almost always had an alternative and the policy converted mass refloats into
rank-1 kills.  Near 1 means the observation graph, not the election, is the binding
constraint and the knob is not worth arming.  The 10-epoch wiring smoke measured 3/21 =
0.14, but 10 cold epochs carry almost no slip traffic and that number cannot be trusted
SECONDARY: chord births / slip refloats per epoch vs runs/churn_base2, and total_IF as
the NO-HARM check.  Do NOT expect med|frac_cyc| or dd_sigma_cyc to move — this card's 3 h
legs already established four times over that churn reduction does not touch them.
